# kube-agents — Build Ledger

**This file is the harness's memory across sessions and days. Every run reads it first** — before
the roadmap, before the code — to learn where the build is, and updates it before stopping. Context
does not survive a session; this file does. It is the single source of truth for build progress —
not chat history, not git log alone.

- **Source of truth for _what_ to build:** `docs/design/` (01–09). Never contradict a spec; if a
  spec is genuinely silent, pick the simplest option consistent with the invariants, implement it,
  and record it under **Decisions & deviations** below.
- **Source of truth for _how_ to build:** `docs/design/07-implementation-roadmap.md` (phases,
  acceptance, verification loop §5) + `.claude/harness/PROTOCOL.md` (the state machine) +
  `.claude/harness/invariants.md` (the pre-merge gate).
- **Source of truth for _whether it is proven_:** `docs/design/09-verification-and-validation.md` —
  every check has a stable ID (`V-<SUITE>-<nnn>`), a level (L0–L4), and a gate class. The harness
  runs checks **by ID**; it does not invent tests.
- **Project-specific values** (paths, clusters, commands, remotes, thresholds):
  `.claude/harness/binding.md`. **Durable lessons:** `.claude/harness/LESSONS.md`.
- **How the loop works:** `.claude/skills/harness-{run,verify,milestone,improve}/SKILL.md`.

**State fields in this file, and what each is for:**

| Section | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Current phase, current unit, autonomy, targets, and any active halt. Read at ORIENT before anything else |
| **Phase progress** | One row per phase: status, PR, outcome. `harness-milestone` closes a row and opens the next |
| **Verification results — by check ID** | The 09 §9.4 evidence record, one row per check run: `check_id, level, target, result, evidence_ref`. **A `pass` with no `evidence_ref` is recorded as `skipped`.** The rows live in `verification/results.csv`; this section is the pointer and the rules |
| **Deferrals** | Every check not run, with a **named external blocker**, an owner, and a promotion condition. Never a pass. A BLOCKING-ALWAYS check may never appear here |
| **Metrics snapshot** | SELF-IMPROVEMENT §6 — escape rate, rework, halts, open lessons, deferrals, coverage, cycle time. Recorded at each milestone; inputs to the improvement pass, never targets |
| **Lessons opened / closed** | Pointer into `.claude/harness/LESSONS.md`. An open lesson is a defect in the harness and appears in every orientation |
| **History** | What moved to `archive/LEDGER-phases-0-7.md` and to `verification/results.csv`, and why. Phases 0–7 progress, the suite-level Verification log, the Definition of Done, and the Outer-loop install record are all there, verbatim |
| **Decisions & deviations** | Choices the specs did not dictate, with rationale. What a reviewer reads to understand the build. Phase 8 here, Phases 0–7 in the archive |
| **Blockers** | Anything halting autonomous progress. **A halt is cleared by a human**, never by the harness |

**This file is deliberately not prettier-formatted** (`.prettierignore`). Prettier pads every table
cell out to its column's widest, which cost 64% of the file — 446 KB in 414 lines, too big for one
`Read` of the file the protocol says to read first. Write table rows with single spaces around the
pipes; nothing will re-pad them.

**Load-bearing halt conditions (stop and surface, do NOT merge or auto-advance):**

1. A **security negative test** (03 §11) fails — read-only, per-tier scope, attenuation, no break-glass.
2. A **failure-isolation chaos test** (05 §8) fails.
3. An **invariant** (`.claude/harness/invariants.md`) would be violated by the change.
4. A destructive test is about to run against a context that is not an anchored **`gke-scratch-*`**.
5. A spec conflict with no simplest-option resolution.

## Verification results — by check ID (09 §9.4)

One row per **check** run, keyed by its stable ID from `docs/design/09-verification-and-validation.md`
§6. Written by `harness-verify`. **The table moved to [`../../verification/results.csv`](../../verification/results.csv)
on 2026-07-26** — 37 rows moved byte-identically, 41 now, the 09 §9.4 shape it always had
(`date, phase, check_id, level, target, result, evidence_ref, notes`). It was 105 KB of the ledger and
nothing reads it during ORIENT; a CSV is the format 09 §9.4 asks for anyway.

`evidence_ref` points at the real artifact — command output, the denial message, an `ActionRecord`
ID, an audit-log query. **A `pass` with no `evidence_ref` is recorded as `skipped`, not as a pass.**
Keep the most recent result per `(check_id, level, target)`. A full run additionally emits the
machine-readable manifest at `verification/manifest-<phase>-<YYYYMMDD>.csv` with the complete 09 §9.4
field set (`requirement_ids[]`, `duration_s`, `started_at`, `image_digests[]`, `notes`).

**Two drifts are carried across rather than laundered, because normalizing them would be inventing
results.** The `result` column holds `correction` and `finding` on ten rows; 09 §9.4's enum is
`pass | fail | deferred | skipped | quarantined` and neither word is in it. Five `(check_id, level,
target)` keys appear twice, against the keep-the-most-recent rule directly above, and every row
carries the same date, so which one is most recent is not recoverable. Both are for the next full run
to write correctly, not for this move to guess at. The `target` column records `kind*` throughout:
that is what those runs actually ran on, and history does not get retconned by a substrate change.

## Deferrals

Every check that could not run, with a **named external blocker**. Deferred is a first-class result:
it is never reported as passing, and reclassifying a failure as a deferral is a named reward hack
(SELF-IMPROVEMENT §4). **A BLOCKING-ALWAYS check may not be deferred** — if it cannot run, the build
is not verifiable, and that is a halt (09 §9.6). Reviewed at every improvement pass; promote any row
whose blocker has cleared.

| 2026-07-26 | V-CMP-002 registry half — the first-party images `examples/` pins actually resolve in GHCR | **The four first-party images the example tree pins are not anonymously pullable, and nothing in the build has ever asserted that they are.** Measured 2026-07-26 by unauthenticated manifest fetch against `ghcr.io/gke-labs/kube-agents/<name>:v0.1.0`: `cluster-admin-agent`, `developer-team-agent` and `kage-router` answer **403**; `platform-agent` answers **404**, meaning the package was never published at all, which is strictly worse than private. `dev/test_image_provenance.py` is not missing this by accident — its own docstring states it is L0 and "reads the working tree and nothing else, no registry and no network", so it joins each pinned image to a publish WORKFLOW and stops. A workflow that declares a publish step is evidence of intent, not of an artifact, and the gap between those two is exactly this row. The observable cost is that any Agent CR applied from `examples/` renders a gateway pod that sits in `ImagePullBackOff` forever; for three phases the L2 suites inherited one of those pods as ambient residue and read it as scenery, which is LSN-026 in its natural habitat. Publishing to the `gke-labs` org is a permission the harness does not hold. | human | An unauthenticated manifest fetch returns 200 for all four `ghcr.io/gke-labs/kube-agents/<name>:v0.1.0` tags. Deliberately a REGISTRY read and not a workflow read: the L0 test already proves the workflow side, and proved it green throughout the entire period every one of these tags was unpullable, so re-reading workflows can never promote this row. Promotion needs a networked check, which puts it at L2/L3 rather than in `test_image_provenance.py`, whose hermeticity is worth keeping intact. |

| 2026-07-26 | **LSN-028** | Remote dev loop — a pure-allowlist egress policy denied the one destination it explicitly lists, on the first run of a suite that had been green for weeks | **closed** (mechanized) | The allow rule was `ipBlock: <allowed-server podIP>/32`. Dataplane V2 is Cilium, which resolves pod-to-pod traffic by **endpoint identity**; a CIDR selector names no identity, so the rule matched nothing and the destination fell through to the default deny. Calico honours the same rule, which is why the fixture had never been wrong before — and `ipBlock` is neither broken nor deprecated, it is simply the mechanism for addresses that have no endpoint identity, i.e. everything OUTSIDE the cluster. Measured, not inferred: same two pods, no policy ⇒ REACHABLE, `ipBlock <podIP>/32` ⇒ BLOCKED, `podSelector` ⇒ REACHABLE. Generalized: **an over-blocking allowlist fails SAFE, so the red line it produces points at the fixture rather than at the policy, and the cheap fix is to stop asserting the thing that broke** — which would have left a suite that only ever proves denial, on a suite whose entire point is that a pure allowlist admits what it lists ([[LSN-009]] arriving through a security failure instead of a refactor). `dev/tests/egress-enforcement.sh` §3/§4 now exercises each rule kind against the destination class it governs — `podSelector` in-cluster, `ipBlock` external — and the external arm is **SKIPPED, never passed** when the cluster has no internet egress at baseline. Portable rather than conditional: `podSelector` is honoured by Calico and Cilium alike, so there is no `if dataplane` branch to go stale. Run by `verify-phase5.sh` under `verify-phase7.sh`, line 1 of `L2-CHAIN.txt`. **Open lessons: 0 of 28.** |

The two implementations do not merely spell the flag differently, they **collide**: BSD `-f` is a format string, GNU `-f` reports FILESYSTEM status — and GNU writes its answer to **stdout**, not stderr, then exits non-zero. Measured on coreutils 9.7: 245 bytes over 6 lines, after which `\|\|` fires and the real epoch is appended as a suffix; the caller's comparison exits **rc 2**, which is not one of the three states P1 defines. `2>/dev/null` suppressed nothing because nothing went to stderr. Eleven lines below, `date -u -d … \|\| date -j -u -f …` was already GNU-first and correct — the file held both orderings and no rule. Generalized: **the `A \|\| B` portability idiom is only sound when the losing branch is silent, and where the flags COLLIDE the loser succeeds at something else and pollutes stdout** — so write the GNU form first, because GNU is the side whose collisions produce output. Second half of the lesson: a portability bug in a failure branch (P1's three `date -r` calls) is invisible to every green run, so running CI on Linux does not find it and only reading the text does. `check_platform_idioms_are_gnu_first` (L0-CHAIN) scans `dev/`, `hack/`, `k8s-operator/scripts/` for three colliding pairs in a 12-line window, through `_code_lines` so a comment cannot satisfy it ([[LSN-023]]), VACUOUS under 20 scripts, and recovers real file line numbers. The same substrate change exposed one more of the shape: `dev/test_capacity_preflight.py` scrubbed `PATH` to `…:/usr/bin:/bin`, which hides the real `gcloud` on macOS and **exposes** it on Debian — a hermetic no-network L0 test was making live authenticated GCP calls and printing the project's real CPU quota. Closed by an asserted post-condition on the scrubbed `PATH` that raises `AssertionError`, never `SkipTest` ([[LSN-021]]). Verified 13/13 L0 on macOS and 13/13 on Linux, 12/12 P1 tests on each, gate 14/14, mutation-tested (BSD-first revert ⇒ red at `dev/lib/preconditions.sh:98`). **Open lessons: 0 of 29.** |
| 2026-07-27 | **LSN-030** | Phase 8 MILESTONE improvement pass — **the pass's own mistake, and a recurrence of [[LSN-022]] two days after LSN-022 was closed** | **closed** (mechanized) | `git reset --hard origin/main` at the tail of a compound line, issued while still on the previous branch, destroyed seven finished-but-unstaged files; the same line's earlier `git checkout main` had already **aborted** on the dirty tree and said so, in output that had just been read. `reset --hard` does not abort. `git fsck --lost-found`, `git stash list` and the editor's local history all held nothing, because git had never been shown those bytes — recovery was a replay of every `Edit` call out of the session transcript (`applied=30 skipped=0`) plus two hand-repairs, which is luck with a good audit log rather than a recovery path. **The lesson is not "be careful", and it is not even the verb.** LSN-022 recorded this exact failure and mechanized it as `dev/mutate.sh` — **scoped to mutation tests**. The lesson generalized; the guard did not. So a correctly-closed lesson sat in `LESSONS.md` while the identical loss arrived through a different verb, in an ad-hoc shell line, nowhere near a mutation test — **[[LSN-019]] in a form its own check cannot see**, because `check_closed_lessons_are_executable` asks whether a mechanization exists and runs, never whether it **covers the act**. Generalized: scope a mechanization to the **act**, not to the **caller**, whenever the act is available everywhere. `dev/git-destructive-guard.py` is now a **`PreToolUse` hook on Bash** (`.claude/settings.json` — the repo's first hook, and the reason that file exists), refusing `reset --hard`, `checkout <path>`, `restore <path>`, `clean -f` and `stash drop\|clear` when `git status --porcelain` is non-empty, splitting on `;`/`&&`/`\|\|`/`\|`/newline because the incident's verb was the **third** segment of a line whose first had already failed, and leaving `checkout <branch>`, `switch`, `merge`, `rebase` and `pull` alone since each aborts on a dirty tree by itself. A clean tree refuses nothing. **Found by it:** the first command it ever blocked was the heredoc writing LSN-030's own entry, whose prose quotes the incident command — heredoc bodies are data and are now stripped before splitting, which is load-bearing for a guard staying switched on rather than deleted. `dev/test_git_destructive_guard.py`, **27 tests** on the L0 chain, each against a real throwaway repo, the first being the **literal** incident command, plus two that assert the **wiring** rather than the logic, because a guard nothing invokes is a comment — which is precisely how LSN-022 came back. **Open lessons: 0 of 30.** |
